quote: I'm reaching out really quick because we got a request you were looking into solar for your home here in Beaverton.
stewart_read: The customer immediately disputes making any request. The rep never grounds the lead source with specificity (form name, date, referral channel) which is exactly the protocol move that reduces suspicion per protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number — instead the vague 'we got a request' framing invites exactly the pushback that follows.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have believed a generic reference to 'a request' was sufficient legitimacy framing for a fast-moving call opener.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to anchor the lead source specifically and immediately when a customer disputes the premise — e.g., naming the form or date — rather than letting the dispute stand unaddressed.

quote: is your credit above the credit? Free. You're calling somebody. It's not free.
stewart_read: This is a legitimacy/scam-anxiety challenge layered on top of a cost objection — the customer is questioning whether 'free' framing is a scam tactic. The rep's response at 01:02 explains installation-fee mechanics but never directly addresses the trust/scam undertone in 'it's not free... you're calling somebody.'

coaching_implication: When a customer conflates cost skepticism with distrust of the call itself, coach the rep to name the legitimacy concern directly before re-explaining pricing mechanics.

quote: This one, I don't have it. No.
stewart_read: This is the customer's own disqualifying answer, and ending the call here is correct procedure under the schema's current hard_dq=true rule for stated credit. However, per qualifiers.credit_qualifier's spencer_operator_note, self-reported credit is unreliable (bureau scores often run 30-50 points higher than what customers believe), so a policy question remains open: is DQ-on-stated-credit costing Ion real deals on this floor.
alternative_hypothesis: If Kenny confirms the closer's actual credit pull is the only valid DQ point, this call would be miscategorized as a hard stop rather than a bookable-pending-pull lead.
coaching_implication: This is not a rep coaching gap — it is a floor-level policy question for the manager to raise with Kenny: should setters DQ on stated credit or pass every lead to the closer's actual pull?
